climate_pressure: Seasonal flooding, storms and altered flood pulses around Tonle Sap.
documented_impact: The ethnography describes increased exposure and reduced fishing access after forced settlement.
fcv_mediator: Eviction and fixed relocation removed households' ability to move with seasonal water and fish.
possible_consequence: Narrower livelihood and mobility options can constrain coping with water variability; no climate-induced violence is inferred.
alternative_explanations: Dams, land development, agricultural change and fishing restrictions also alter hydrology and access; climate contributions are not isolated.
uncertainty: Historical three-community ethnography, not a representative causal estimate. Reverse interaction concerns coercive relocation and exclusion, not armed-conflict classification.
resilience_factors: Seasonal mobility was an existing coping practice whose loss is central to the account.
compact_statement: Forced settlement of Tonle Sap floating communities restricted seasonal mobility and fishing access, increasing vulnerability to water variability.
